Detailed Explanation: binary 11111111, where all bits are set. Since the bit position is fixed at 0, the least significant bit is 1. The test verifies that the getBit function correctly extracts this bit and returns 1.
binary 00000000, where no bits are set. The bit at position 0 is 0, so the function should return 0. This verifies correct behavior when the input has no bits set.
binary 00000010. The least significant bit (bit 0) is 0, even though other bits are set. This test ensures the function correctly extracts only the specified bit and returns 0.
binary 00000001, where only the least significant bit is set. The function should return 1, confirming correct extraction of bit 0 when it is set alone.
binary 11111110, where all bits except bit 0 are set. The function should return 0, verifying that it correctly identifies the least significant bit as cleared even when other bits are set.
